svg.title: macOS · Import from Device · pairing code · 460×520
svg.desc: Mirrors Remote/ImportWindow.swift (enteringCode / connecting phases) over Shared/ProjectTransferClient.swift and Shared/CaptureRemotePairing.swift. The six digits shown in Projects on the serving device (iOS/projects.sharing.portrait.svg) are typed here. The code is never the key: it is stretched with HKDF-SHA256 into a TLS-PSK, under a PURPOSE-SCOPED salt ("com.regularsteven.letslapse.transfer.v1") so a code minted for the camera remote cannot be replayed against the library and vice versa — CaptureRemotePairing.derivedKey/parameters take the salt as a defaulted argument, leaving the capture link's wire behaviour bit-identical. The same call also asks for transfer-shaped TCP: keepalive 20/3/5 instead of the control link's 5/2/2, because 5/2/2 tears down a healthy forty-minute pull the moment a congested network stalls it, and Nagle is left ON since bulk chunks fill segments by themselves. THE TRAP THIS SCREEN IS BUILT AROUND: a wrong code never fails the client. It surfaces as -9846 bad MAC on the SERVER's first read and this side sits in .preparing forever — verified again for this link on 2026-08-27, and previously for the camera remote. So the client runs LocalNetworkTransport's 8-second timeout verbatim and reports "Incorrect code — try again" rather than leaving a window that does nothing. The last line is not decoration: one code opens the whole library, not the project you were looking at, and the serving side says the same thing. Connecting state (drawn as a variant of this file's own button): the field disables, the button reads "Pairing…" and a small spinner sits beside it. **2026-09-06 — THE CAMERA.** Under the field, a live viewport that reads the QR the serving device draws beside its code (App/PairingQR.swift). It is a shortcut past TYPING, not past pairing: the scanned code goes through the same connect(to:code:) a typed one does, gets the same PSK-derived TLS, and is remembered on success the same way — so the next visit to that device pairs silently whichever way the first one went. The payload is `LLXFER1:<code>` and carries the code ALONE, because the serving device's identity is derivable from it: CaptureRemotePairing.pairingID(code:) is the same hash that device advertises in its TXT record, so a scan is checked against the device already picked BEFORE the network is touched. A QR from another device, or one photographed before the code rotated, fails that check locally and says so ("That code is for a different device, or it has changed since the code was shown.") rather than presenting as a pairing failure ten seconds later. Three states beyond the live picture, desc-only: no camera on this machine ("No camera available on this device."), access refused ("LetsLapse needs camera access to scan a pairing code. Type the code instead, or turn the camera on in Settings."), and this device shooting, where the viewport is replaced outright by one line rather than opening a second capture session under a running shoot. The phone draws the same screen: iOS/library-import.code.portrait.svg. Verified 2026-08-27; staged with LL_TRANSFER=<6-digit code>, which types the real code rather than bypassing it.

g.text: Shown in Projects on iPhone 17 Pro, while sharing is on.
The code grants access to every project on that device, not just one.
Or scan the QR code shown beside it
